html:
SMTO-LLM-0019 — The model didn't finish its reply properly

GUID: ffb91580-6653-4102-bb02-e31d714e373c
Slug: native-protocol-incomplete
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model's reply ended without the signal that it was complete, or a short setup step, such as choosing tools for a task, ran out of time. SMTO can't act on an unfinished reply, so nothing was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. This quick test shows whether the model server is answering normally right now.
  2. If this keeps happening as a task starts, expand Limits and recovery on the same card, raise Capability selection timeout, and select Save Main. That timeout limits how long the model may take to choose tools for a task.
  3. When the check passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). SMTO never acted on the unfinished reply, so continuing is safe and earlier finished steps are kept.

What success looks like

  • The task continues and the model's next reply is accepted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server; the details include the reason the model gave for stopping. Don't delete SMTO's data or turn off its safety checks to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider's turn did not form one complete assistant decision: a finish reason other than tool_calls or stop, a missing, error-reporting or malformed response envelope, an unfinished response that could not be continued, a non-streamed body over 32 MiB, or an expired internal-phase generation deadline; no operation was authorized (native_protocol_incomplete / native_protocol).

What this means

  • Turn validation requires a supported terminal response; an unfinished finish reason or an expired constrained-generation deadline cannot supply one. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Turn validation requires a supported terminal response; an unfinished finish reason or an expired constrained-generation deadline cannot supply one.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the retained finish reason with the generation deadline and recovery profile; a deadline event differs from a provider returning an unfinished turn.

How to fix it

  • Check the error message plus finish_reason, continuation_unavailable_reason, duration_seconds and threshold_seconds in provider_diagnostic. For an unexpected finish reason or malformed envelope (for example a content filter, a missing reason or an error object), check provider logs and native tool-call support; for an expired deadline, raise the role's Capability selection timeout or Recovery deadline in Settings › Setup › Model routing. Earlier receipts are unaffected; resume after the fix.
  • Check the provider logs and native tool-call support before resuming.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A subsequent authorized decision reaches a valid terminal response without crossing its effective generation deadline.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
